rationales.A: Neither crisis had a single cause. Both mixed domestic weakness with wider economic trouble.
rationales.B: The order is reversed. Hoover resisted direct federal relief, and the New Deal came in 1933, while Cleveland’s government in 1893 also did little.
rationales.C: The 1893 panic was a railroad-and-bank crisis met by a limited government. Background: the 1929 crash collapsed a credit economy and produced the Depression, and the New Deal that followed permanently expanded the federal government’s economic role.
rationales.D: The 1929 crash was followed by thousands of bank failures between 1930 and 1933. The banks were not untouched.
rationales.general:
1. Name the 1893 crisis. A railroad and bank panic, met by a government that believed relief was not its job.
2. Name the 1929 economy. Stocks bought on margin and goods bought on credit, so the fall reached every household.
3. Compare the aftermaths. After 1893 the government did little; after 1929 the Depression forced the New Deal and a permanent safety net.
4. Put it together. The difference is not the panic but what it hit and what the government finally did about it.
Remember: comparing two crises means comparing what came after them, not only what caused them.
